Real Estate

Housing decisions, connected end to end

A home is often both the largest purchase and the largest single asset a household owns. These guides walk the decision tree: rent versus buy on an after-tax basis, how much house a budget can sustain, how to buy or rent on purpose, what changes when the property is an investment, and how to downsize or relocate in the 45–65 years.

There is no universal winner. Every guide labels assumptions, links official IRS and CFPB sources for tax and mortgage rules, and points to the next step that fits your situation.

Common questions

Should I rent or buy?

Compare equal cash flows and after-tax terminal wealth. Factor investment capital gains, the main-home sale exclusion if you qualify ($250,000 / $500,000), amortization, leverage, and labeled home-price scenarios — not a guaranteed rise.

  • Should I Rent or Buy? After-Tax Wealth, Not Just the Payment

How much house can I afford?

Separate lender approval from a sustainable all-in payment (PITI, HOA, PMI, maintenance, reserves). Stress-test income drops and retirement contributions, especially at 45–65.

  • How Much House Can I Afford? Lender Max vs Sustainable Budget

What should I check when buying a primary home?

Compare Loan Estimates and the Closing Disclosure, keep key contingencies, and verify inspections, title, flood risk, insurance, taxes and HOA reserves before you waive protections.

  • Buying a Primary Home

Should I downsize or relocate?

Net out selling costs and confirm IRS main-home exclusion eligibility, then price the next home or rental against healthcare access, taxes and retirement cash needs. Renting first in a new area reduces costly mistakes.

  • Downsizing or Relocating at 45–65
  • Money at 55 to 59

Is a rental property a good investment?

Underwrite cash flow after vacancy, repairs, capex and debt service. Cap rate is not a personal return promise. Read IRS Publications 527 and 925 for depreciation and passive-loss themes, and do not assume the main-home exclusion applies.

  • Investment Property
  • Real Estate vs. Stocks

What is the housing market doing?

Headline numbers can point in opposite directions. Use FHFA price data and articles that explain what each series measures.
